summary: Node22/Express library borrowing gateway: a single deployable service exposing Catalog and Loans business modules over a REST API backed by PostgreSQL16, plus a plain HTML/CSS/JS browser UI. Borrowing and returning use transactions with row locks on a single client; returns are idempotent. Unit tests run against an injected in-memory adapter (no live Postgres); real PostgreSQL behavior is exercised by the runtime HTTP acceptance. Delivery includes OpenAPI, Compose (gateway:3000, postgres:5432), Dockerfile, schema, plan, and source-to-test traceability.

tasks.description: Idempotent PostgreSQL schema bootstrap and seeding. books (id, title, copies, availableCopies) and loans (id, bookId, userId, status). Seed idempotently; never overwrite user-created books.
Catalog business module: create book (positive integer copies), list books, get book by id. Validation and 404 handling.
Loans business module: borrow (transaction, lock book row, validate stock + active loan, decrement available, insert loan) and idempotent return (increment stock exactly once).
Repository/store interface with two implementations: PostgresStore (production, transactional row-lock semantics) and InMemoryStore (test-only adapter, no fallback in production).
Express app wiring: routes for /api/books, /api/books/:id, /api/loans, /api/loans/:id/return, /health, and static / UI. Correct status codes 201/200/400/404/409.
Server entrypoint selecting PostgresStore, honoring PUBLIC_ORIGIN for redirects and OIDC_ISSUER/OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN env passthrough for gateway.
Plain HTML/CSS/JS page at / listing books/available copies, entering reader ID, borrowing, returning loans, success/error feedback.
Unit tests (no live Postgres) for catalog, loans semantics, idempotent return, concurrency-on-memory, and HTTP routes via injected memory adapter.
Compose (gateway:3000 with /health, postgres:5432), Dockerfile (node:22, healthcheck script path aligns with package.json).
package.json with pinned deps, test/build/start/healthcheck scripts.

assumptions: ASM1: Reader IDs (userId) are demonstration caller-provided inputs, not authenticated identities, per the operator supplement; no OAuth/identity code is implemented.

ASM2: Unit tests use an injected in-memory adapter (dependency injection) so `npm test` requires no live PostgreSQL. Production code (npm start / Docker) always uses PostgreSQL and never falls back to in-memory, satisfying the 'no in-memory persistence when PostgreSQL is unavailable' constraint.

ASM3: availableCopies is stored and read directly to keep catalog reads cheap; total copies is stored separately. Borrow decrements availableCopies, return increments it exactly once (idempotency enforced by loan status, not by counting calls).
ASM4: Loan status values are active/returned matching the state machine; returning an already-returned loan returns the same 200 with no stock change.

ASM5: The 'roughly 12-18 files' supplement target is treated as a source-conciseness hint; mandatory delivery artifacts (openapi.yaml, plan.json, traceability.json, architecture-decisions.md, compose.yaml, Dockerfile) are required by the host and increase total file count.

ASM6: PUBLIC_ORIGIN controls browser-facing redirect construction; OIDC_ISSUER and OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN are read/forwarded as gateway public-URL environment variables even though no OAuth flows are implemented.
ASM7: SQL identifiers and JSON keys are camelCase to match the fixed REST contract (availableCopies, bookId, userId).
conflicts: CONFLICT1: Operator supplement states 'no in-memory persistence when PostgreSQL is unavailable' while the host requires `npm test` to run without a live PostgreSQL. Resolved via ASSUMPTION ASM2: DI-backed test adapter vs production-only PostgresStore; no silent in-memory fallback at runtime.

CONFLICT2: Operator supplement requests 'roughly 12-18 files' but the host mandates at least plan.json, traceability.json, architecture-decisions.md, openapi.yaml, compose.yaml, Dockerfile, package.json, README.md plus source/tests. Resolved in favor of host requirements; noted in ASM5.

CONFLICT3: Original design does not mention seeding; supplement asks for 'idempotent schema creation/seed'. Resolved: seed only inserts when tables are empty, never overwriting or duplicating user-created books.
